placement_after: Buddy put a neatly folded blanket from Chirag’s gang beside a small clay bowl from the elderly chaiwala who always saved him an extra biscuit. When Neet tried to add a mango pit to the blanket, Buddy moved the bowl on top. These were coming home intact.
alt_text: Neet guards his improbable souvenirs while Buddy keeps his clay bowl and blanket safely separate.
scene_brief: Packing at home before leaving India. Open suitcase at left holds a carefully folded cloth, small brass diya and painted kite visible. Neet stands beside his repurposed tote, one paw possessively braced beside FOUR chewed mango pits, tiny sunglasses, a rolled poster with no readable words and one napkin-wrapped pani-puri shell. Buddy at right gently plants a front paw beside a small CLAY BOWL resting on his neatly folded special blanket, blocking Neet from adding a mango pit. Both full bodies grounded, no paw fingers, compact toes, short smooth coats, Neet tiny nub, Buddy low dark taper. Their gazes meet: treasure-hoarding Neet and calmly protective Buddy. No human figures. Funny assortment with genuinely meaningful bowl/blanket, no airport or food hidden in fur. This shared packing beat suits primary and its lounge-omission alternative.
